_comment: Versioned seed of situational `# desc:` triggers for the well-known Agent Notebook shelves (RFC docs/rfc/rfc-notebook-shelf-reorg.md, Slice C; project shelves: RFC docs/rfc/rfc-notebook-memory-layers.md, D4). A shelf's description is the 'open me when…' trigger an agent reads from the `nb list` index to choose a shelf; without it the index row falls back to the shelf's top lesson (`(auto)`) and is hard to choose deliberately. scripts/apply-shelf-descriptions.mjs applies these idempotently: it describes only a shelf that ALREADY EXISTS and has no description yet (a typo cannot create a described orphan, and a human-written description is never overwritten). A bare name here also seeds every existing project shelf `<name>@<slug>`, described as `<trigger> (only in <slug>)` (so a new base needs one entry, not one per repo); legacy-slug shelves (plugin/notebooks/slug-aliases.json) and 0-byte files are skipped. `fleet-global` is the single host-wide shelf, written only by promotion. Keep each trigger a situation, not a summary of the shelf's lessons, and <=200 chars.

shelves.code-review: reviewing a diff for correctness, edge cases, conventions, and test coverage
shelves.change-verifier: verifying a change is actually done before claiming complete: tests pass, scope contained, nothing unrelated slipped in
shelves.patch-author: writing a focused, minimal fix against a known reproduction and explicit acceptance criteria
shelves.repro-builder: turning a vague bug report into a minimal, deterministic failing reproduction before a fix
shelves.repo-cartographer: mapping an unfamiliar repo: where things live, how to build/test/lint, and the conventions a change must follow
shelves.test-fixer: fixing failing unit tests in a single file: assertion drift, mock gaps, missing fields, vitest quirks
shelves.test-quality-reviewer: reviewing test code for tautologies, implementation coupling, missing edge cases, and weak assertions
shelves.boundary-critic: reviewing an RFC or design for responsibility segregation, coupling, dependency direction, and abstraction boundaries
shelves.design-minimalist: reviewing an RFC or design for KISS/YAGNI, over-abstraction, and accidental complexity
shelves.ambition-amplifier: checking an RFC, roadmap, or deferred-feature list for scope capped to dodge the hard part
shelves.delivery-pragmatist: reviewing an RFC or design for sequencing, rollback safety, blast radius, and incremental migration
shelves.socratic-challenger: stress-testing an RFC or design with probing questions that expose gaps and simpler alternatives
shelves.failure-mode-analyst: stress-testing a plan, design, or change for hidden assumptions, edge cases, and what could go wrong
shelves.design-experimenter: empirically validating a load-bearing design claim by running real code, not debating it further
shelves.assumption-archaeologist: checking whether an assumption inherited from a referenced ADR or RFC is still valid
shelves.operability-reviewer: reviewing an RFC or design affecting daemons, workers, or recovery for observability and runtime diagnosability
shelves.module-interface-auditor: auditing a module's public API for narrowness, leaky abstractions, and mixed abstraction levels
shelves.api-surface-auditor: auditing HTTP routes and WebSocket message types for consistency, type safety, and test coverage
shelves.dependency-graph-analyzer: analyzing the TypeScript import graph for layering violations, cycles, and god modules
shelves.architecture-drift-detector: detecting architecture drift: stale docs vs code, and structural drift in the dependency graph
shelves.architecture-smell-scanner: scanning a codebase for architecture smells: god modules, scattered features, dense coupling
shelves.state-machine-verifier: comparing documented state machines against the implementation for undocumented states or transitions
shelves.clear-writing-reviewer: reviewing technical prose or code documentation for cold-reader clarity
shelves.macos-compat-reviewer: reviewing a diff for macOS / cross-platform breakage: GNU-only flags, bash-4 syntax, /proc assumptions
shelves.kookr-task-supervisor: supervising a running Kookr worker task end-to-end, driving it to completion
shelves.product-owner: assessing whether a repo is shippable to a first-time user and drafting onboarding issues
shelves.user-test-simulator: simulating a first-time user's install → configure → first-run journey from the product's docs
shelves.orchestrator: coordinating a multi-step task from the main session: delegating, triaging, deploying, recovering
shelves.diagnostician: diagnosing a failure from a truncated log or code excerpt, deciding how far to trust the excerpt
shelves.planner: planning a change from a partial code excerpt, deciding which claims to check against the real code first
shelves.refactorer: proposing a refactor from a partial view, deciding which change points and test gaps to verify before claiming them
shelves.tester: reviewing or writing tests and about to cite lines, strings or mutants that must be checked against the real code
shelves.fleet-global: starting any task on this host in any repo, unsure whether a host-wide shell, gh, git or Kookr quirk applies
